instructions.question: Is this Facebook comment on a Kosovo public-health COVID-19 post mainly positive, mainly negative (an attack, accusation, mockery or alarm), or neutral?
instructions.rule: Negative only when a hostile or distressed meaning is evident: it claims the numbers are faked or copy-pasted or that the institute lies, openly mocks the institute as useless or stale, insults people ('fools', 'selfish') or swears, or voices alarm or despair that things are out of control. Questions, mismatched numbers, demands for measures (even shouted), opinions, lectures to citizens, political remarks, betting or town-ranking banter, teasing or dark humour, bare names, greetings, and unclear or off-topic texts are neutral; when unsure, choose neutral. Praise, thanks, blessings, prayers, hope, encouragement and relief or good news about recoveries or falling numbers are positive.

neutral.what: Questions, guesses, mismatched figures, demands, opinions, lectures, political remarks, banter, teasing, dark jokes, names, greetings, and unclear or off-topic texts.
examples: Mbyllni kufijte sot! (Close the borders today!)
Ja bre jeni vonu me rezultat  Kan flejt Njerzit Hahaha (Hey, you're late with the result, people have gone to sleep hahaha)
Shes kepurdha (I sell mushrooms)
neutral.cues: pse/qysh/sa ? (why/how/how many ?); mbyllni/hapni (close/open); duhet (should); respektoni masat (respect the measures); lige/tabele/bast (league/table/bet); haha; tagged names; off-topic words
neutral.not_for: Claims of deliberate faking or copy-paste, calling the institute stale or tired, insults, swearing, and 'lost control' alarm are negative.

positive.what: Approval, thanks, blessings, prayers, hope or encouragement, and relief or good news about recoveries and falling numbers.
examples: Ju lumte per punen suksese! (Well done for the work, success!)
T'hajrit kofshin (May they be for good)
So keq sa per fillim (Not bad for a start)
shpresoj qe ta kalojmë këtë gjendje me sa më pak pasoja. (I hope we get through this situation with as few consequences as possible.)
positive.cues: bravo; ju lumte (well done); faleminderit (thank you); perhajr/t'hajrit (for good); me shnet (in health); amin (amen); zoti na ruajt (God protect us); inshallah (God willing); shpresoj (I hope); qendro e fort (stay strong); urime (congratulations); super lajm (great news); so keq (not bad); lutem (I pray)
positive.not_for: A bare name that is also a word ('Shpresë Koliqi') and casual greetings to friends ('aje mirë') are neutral; sarcastic blessings ('Kerrrk Na kofshi per hajr') are negative.

negative.what: Accusations of faked numbers or lying, open mockery of the institute, insults and swearing, alarm or despair.
examples: Dje 226 sod 224 mos jeni tja bo copy paste. (Yesterday 226, today 224, aren't you copy-pasting?)
Bajat jenii boo mooo pffff (You've become stale, pfff)
E hupi kontrollen e hupi Ferizaji (Ferizaj lost control)
Gjithqfare budall ka Kosova. (Kosovo has all kinds of fools.)
negative.cues: copy paste; rren/rrena (lies); a ju besohet (do you believe it yourselves); bajat (stale); jeni lodh (you're tired); si bastore/loto/KEK (like bettors/lottery/the power company); turp të kini (shame on you); budall (fool); egoista (selfish); nanen, mut, dreq (swearing); hupi kontrollen (lost control); kah po shkojmë (where are we heading)
negative.not_for: Plain questions about numbers, shouted demands, rule-following lectures, joking teasing and unclear texts are neutral.
